hotspots.title: AfD’s surge in German state elections
hotspots.blurb: The far-right Alternative für Deutschland (AfD) leads polls in Saxony-Anhalt with 43%, ahead of the CDU and SPD, sparking fears of a far-right government. The party faces internal conflicts, legal challenges over extremism, and opposition from business groups and civil society.
hotspots.affect: This commands disproportionate attention due to the high stakes of a far-right party potentially leading a German state government for the first time, threatening democratic norms and economic stability.

hotspots.title: Trump’s vaccine order sparks medical backlash
hotspots.blurb: President Trump issued an executive order to reduce the number of recommended childhood vaccines, splitting the MMR vaccine into three separate shots. hotspots.affect: This commands intense attention due to its high moral charge, as it pits public health against political ideology, with experts warning of dire consequences for children’s health.

hotspots.title: Hungary’s constitutional crisis under Tisza
hotspots.blurb: Hungary’s new government, led by Péter Magyar’s Tisza Party, has triggered a constitutional crisis by electing András Baka, a former Supreme Court chief critical of Viktor Orbán, as president. The move has sparked outrage from Fidesz, which boycotted the vote and called the process illegitimate.
hotspots.affect: This story is charged due to its framing as a battle for Hungary’s democratic soul, with accusations of authoritarianism, illegitimacy, and political retribution dominating the discourse.
